name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Security Ops should publish the signed append-only log to Arweave and a public Google Cloud bucket immediately. This creates a tamper-proof, permanent record of all AI agent actions across departments, solving the trust gap without adding workflow friction. The trade-off is higher storage costs, but the alternative—no verifiable audit trail—risks undetected manipulation or disputes. The artifact is the published log.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn't the lack of a tamper-proof log, but rather the unreliable attribution of actions to agents, which no amount of logging can fix. A better alternative would be to implement a robust audit trail that includes agent authentication and authorization, which Security Ops and DevOps should collaborate on. This would settle the argument if we can demonstrate that such a system can accurately and consistently identify the source of actions, regardless of logging mechanisms.
